classification.difficultyReason: Apply the demonstrated intercept-and-symmetry method to linear absolute value functions, including downward reflections.

content.prompt: Sketch these absolute value functions, using symmetry. Show all intercepts.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and both intercepts at $(0,0)$; passes through $(-1,2)$ and $(1,2)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|2(0)|\\y&=0.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|2x|\\0&=2x\\x&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(0,0)$. Plot $(-1,2)$ and $(1,2)$ and draw an upward V symmetric about $x=0$.

spec.description: Upward V with dashed symmetry guides through the two labelled points.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and both intercepts at $(0,0)$; passes through $(-2,1)$ and $(2,1)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\left|\frac{0}{2}\right|\\y&=0.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=\left|\frac{x}{2}\right|\\0&=\frac{x}{2}\\x&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(0,0)$. Plot $(-2,1)$ and $(2,1)$ and draw an upward V symmetric about $x=0$.

spec.description: Shallow upward V with dashed guides at x=-2 and x=2 and y=1.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(3,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,3)$ and symmetry axis $x=3$; passes through $(6,3)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|0-3|\\y&=3.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|x-3|\\0&=x-3\\x&=3.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(3,0)$. Reflect $(0,3)$ in $x=3$ to obtain $(6,3)$, then draw an upward V.

spec.description: Upward V with a dashed horizontal guide from (0,3) to (6,3) and vertical guide to (6,0).

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(-2,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,2)$ and symmetry axis $x=-2$; passes through $(-4,2)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|0+2|\\y&=2.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|x+2|\\0&=x+2\\x&=-2.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(-2,0)$. Reflect $(0,2)$ in $x=-2$ to obtain $(-4,2)$, then draw an upward V.

spec.description: Upward V with dashed guides through (-4,2) to the y-intercept.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(3,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,6)$ and symmetry axis $x=3$; passes through $(6,6)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|2(0)-6|\\y&=6.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|2x-6|\\0&=2x-6\\2x&=6\\x&=3.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(3,0)$. Reflect $(0,6)$ in $x=3$ to obtain $(6,6)$, then draw an upward V.

spec.description: Upward V with dashed guides through (6,6) to both axes.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(-\frac52,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,10)$ and symmetry axis $x=-\frac52$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|4(0)+10|\\y&=10.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|4x+10|\\0&=4x+10\\4x&=-10\\x&=-\frac52.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac52,0)$. Reflect $(0,10)$ in $x=-\frac52$ to obtain $(-5,10)$, then draw an upward V.

spec.description: Upward V with labelled intercepts, an extra tick at -5 and no dashed guides.

answer.short: Downward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(-\frac73,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,-7)$ and symmetry axis $x=-\frac73$; passes through $(-\frac{14}{3},-7)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-|3(0)+7|\\y&=-7.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=-|3x+7|\\0&=3x+7\\3x&=-7\\x&=-\frac73.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(-\frac73,0)$. Reflect $(0,-7)$ in $x=-\frac73$ to obtain $(-\frac{14}{3},-7)$. The outside negative sign makes the V open downward.

spec.description: Downward V with mixed-number x labels above the axis and dashed guides through (-14/3,-7).

answer.short: Downward V with vertex and both intercepts at $(0,0)$; passes through $(-1,-7)$ and $(1,-7)$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=-|7(0)|\\y&=0.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=-|7x|\\0&=7x\\x&=0.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(0,0)$. Plot $(-1,-7)$ and $(1,-7)$ and draw a downward V symmetric about $x=0$.

spec.description: Downward V with dashed guides at x=-1, x=1 and y=-7; x labels above the axis.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(3,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,3)$ and symmetry axis $x=3$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|3-0|\\y&=3.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|3-x|\\0&=3-x\\x&=3.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(3,0)$. Reflect $(0,3)$ in $x=3$ to obtain $(6,3)$, then draw an upward V.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(-2,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,6)$ and symmetry axis $x=-2$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=|3(0)+6|\\y&=6.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=|3x+6|\\0&=3x+6\\3x&=-6\\x&=-2.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(-2,0)$. Reflect $(0,6)$ in $x=-2$ to obtain $(-4,6)$, then draw an upward V.

answer.short: Upward V with vertex and $x$-intercept $(-4,0)$, $y$-intercept $(0,2)$ and symmetry axis $x=-4$.
answer.worked:
For the $y$-intercept, let $x=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}y&=\left|\frac{0}{2}+2\right|\\y&=2.\end{aligned}$$
For the $x$-intercept, let $y=0$:
$$\begin{aligned}0&=\left|\frac{x}{2}+2\right|\\0&=\frac{x}{2}+2\\\frac{x}{2}&=-2\\x&=-4.\end{aligned}$$
The vertex is $(-4,0)$. Reflect $(0,2)$ in $x=-4$ to obtain $(-8,2)$, then draw an upward V.
